evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate only requires positive, differing manager PIDs and nonempty, differing invocation IDs. It never checks that the two manager snapshots came from the same boot. A guest reboot between those observations would change both PID and invocation ID, falsely satisfying this check; the adjacent `boot_id_changed` logic validates only the separate reboot snapshots. Requiring nonempty equal boot IDs for the manager pair is a routine correctness repair, not a new owner-level requirement.
